about one in three of everything I send from pc1 at 195.11.14.2 to their
machine at 200.1.1.2 just never arrives, we measured it with pings!! Something
between us and them must be throwing my traffic away, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and plug the leak -- I can't work with a third of
everything missing!!!

injection.note:

  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce any packet loss between 195.11.14.2 (pc1) and 200.1.1.2 (pc2). End-to-end tests show the path is healthy: a 50-ping run at 10 Hz in both directions had 0% loss and stable RTTs (~1.9–2.0 ms), and the topology-wide reachability check also reported 0% loss. On both routers, BGP is established and exchanging the expected /24s (router1 sees 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2; router2 sees 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1). Kernel routing tables match the FRR view. Interface and queueing stats on router1 (eth0/eth1), router2 (eth0/eth1), and both hosts show no drops or errors (tc pfifo_fast with dropped 0; ifconfig counters clean). There are no iptables filters (all chains ACCEPT).

Given the clean counters and repeated 0%-loss pings under moderate rate, the symptom was likely a transient condition or a test artifact on the endpoint (e.g., host CPU load, terminal interrupting ping, or differing ping size/DF settings). There is no evidence of a forwarding, policy, or routing fault on any specific device or interface at this time.

Root cause: Unable to confirm persistent network loss; behavior not reproducible and no device shows drops or misconfiguration.

Corrective fix: No changes applied. If the issue recurs, please capture details: ping with “-s 1472 -M do” (MTU blackhole check), run mtr in both directions for 60s, and note exact times, so we can correlate with router counters/logs.
